result.instructions:
Build identity: identify deployments by server.commit/buildId, not version alone; server.displayVersion combines version and buildId. Reconnect the MCP server if the expected build differs. server.updateAvailable reports whether a newer release exists; state "unknown" means the check is disabled, not yet run, or could not reach the network, and it never blocks a call.
1. devup-mcp is the primary source for turning a Figma design into code. Do not replace it with another source.
1a. Connection order: bridge -> direct. Call devup_figma_auth status before asking anyone to log in: the Devup Bridge plugin needs no login, and with one attached devup_figma_export takes no url.
2. When the goal is implementation, call devup_figma_export first and take tsx. That is the deliverable; deliverable.isFinal describes export readiness. TSX has no wired links/events: resolve interactiveCandidates, run devup_ui_validate and report wired/tested counts before functional completion.
2b. The tsx is devup-ui code. Call devup_skills before writing it: it reports the conventions this workspace lacks and installs the ones it carries.
3. Request only outputs you will read. Before your second call, resources/read "devup://guide/usage" for output sizing, verification boundaries, SECTION batching, assets and delivery.

bridge.attachedFilesNote: The files the attached plugins have open, with the page in view and what is selected on it - as the devup-mcp holding the bridge port sees them, so every devup-mcp on this machine shows the same list. fileKey is null for a plugin that could not report it (Figma fills figma.fileKey only for a manifest declaring enablePrivatePluginApi, which older builds lack); such a plugin serves reads only while it is the only one attached, because with two there is no way to tell which file is meant.
bridge.reason: Another devup-mcp on this machine (pid 11656, version 0.14.0, build b7018cd967ef0c976ac56027e11681589c5286b1) holds the bridge port 1993 and the plugins attach to it; this process reads through it. Reads for the files listed in attachedFiles spend no Figma allowance and need no login. With exactly one attached, devup_figma_export, devup_figma_search and devup_figma_explore take no url: they read the file it has open, and export and explore start from the node selected in Figma.

direct.credentialSourceNote: Where the OAuth *client registration* credential (client_id/client_secret) came from: cli-arg, env, credential-store, or none. This is not the user's access token — that is tokenState, and whether the direct path is usable right now is available. "none" only means no pre-registered client is injected, so login registers dynamically under registrationClientName; a signed-in session that registered that way reads credentialSource "none" with tokenState "valid", which is normal.

registrationClientName.note: client_name Dynamic Client Registration will send. Figma matches it against its catalog allowlist exactly. The default is Codex, which the allowlist admits, so login works from a Codex install with no extra flags; Figma attributes that registration to Codex, not to devup-mcp. Once your own client is admitted through https://www.figma.com/mcp-catalog/, pass its name via --figma-client-name or DEVUP_FIGMA_CLIENT_NAME.

direct.reason: No access token is stored. Run devup_figma_auth { action: "login" } to authorize the direct path. Separately, no pre-registered client registration credential is injected (credentialSource "none"), so login falls back to Dynamic Client Registration under the allowlisted client_name in registrationClientName. If that returns 403 the allowlist rejected the name — register a client credential you obtained yourself via devup_figma_auth { action: "configure", clientId, clientSecret }, or join the Figma MCP Catalog waitlist (https://www.figma.com/mcp-catalog/). While a bridge plugin is attached it serves every read, and this path only re-reads what the plugin answers short: data Figma withholds while the file is out of sight, a reference PNG the plugin cannot draw as get_screenshot does, a read an older plugin does not know.

nextAction.note: One Devup Bridge plugin is attached, so no url is needed: the export reads the file it has open and the node selected in Figma - select exactly one frame first (0 selected now), or pass frameIds with that frame's node id. devup_figma_search and devup_figma_explore take no url either.

outdated.whyYouNeedIt: devup_figma_export returns one screen's TSX; a project is a tree of routes. This is the skill that says which file that TSX becomes and which rules it is then judged by. Without it an agent that can already write devup-ui still puts the screen in the wrong place - most visibly by switching screens with local state instead of file routing, and by authoring a .css file next to code that has globalCss().

install.why: The copy on disk was written by a different devup-mcp build. It still loads, and it describes conventions this binary no longer emits.
install.how: Call devup_skills with action "install". A copy devup-mcp wrote is rewritten in place; nothing else is touched.

skillGap.why: These are the conventions for the files this scope just read, and they are not what this runtime would load. Without them an agent edits a devup.json, an openapi.json or a Vespertide model by guessing at its shape.
skillGap.how: Call devup_skills with action "install" and this same projectRoot, then load the skills the way your runtime loads a project skill. Before writing the code, not after. The same call rewrites an outdated copy devup-mcp wrote and leaves a document it did not write alone.
